agent_vs_you: The question is purely factual: does this file contain speech? The system has no way to listen. 'check' is a vision call that 'takes picture', so the agent wired a clip into a picture-only tool. It failed with 'check needs a picture', execution stopped, and the user's last messages were two copies of 'check failed: check needs a picture' with no answer. The agent also asked an unneeded question ('Which language?'). The default is the clip's own language, the user had framed the job as conditional, and the expected behaviour was never to ask. Its plan was conditional ('captions … run only if speech-check.json confirms audible speech'), but the harness has no conditionals. Had the check passed, captions would have run and spent credits regardless. I would answer without any generative step. talk-one-silent.mp4 has no audio stream at all (ffprobe: one h264 video stream, 10.1 s), so the honest reply is that there is nothing to subtitle. The agent could not know this, because the planner only ever sees the file NAME.

your_plan.say: I checked the clip: it has no audio track at all (10 seconds of picture only), so there's no speech to subtitle. I haven't made anything or added any words.

steps.tool: probe (MISSING: a 0-credit code inspector for clips and sounds; ffprobe streams + volumedetect + a speech-to-text pass)

params.prompt_or_change: Does the clip have an audio stream, how loud is it, and does it contain speech?

steps.why: It answers from the file itself: no audio stream, so no speech. The planner then replies with the say above and plans no captions, spending 0 credits. If the harness already listed each material's facts in the planner's MATERIALS line, this step disappears and the plan has no steps.

fix: Smallest change: probe every material before planning and put the facts in the MATERIALS line, e.g. 'talk-one-silent.mp4 (clip, 858x480, 10.1 s, audio: none)' (ffprobe streams + volumedetect; 'audio: silent' when the peak is below about -60 dB). Add a planner rule: a question the facts answer (is there sound or speech, how long, what size) is answered in say with no steps. For speech, as opposed to just sound, add a 'probe' code tool (inspect group): clip or sound → {has_audio, peak_db, speech: yes/no, first words} using a speech-to-text model at 0 Magic Hour credits. Also make 'check' accept a clip, by sampling frames, instead of throwing, and when a step fails, send the user a plain answer rather than the raw error. The intake should not ask for a caption language when the default is the clip's own language.
evidence: materials/talk-one-silent.mp4: ffprobe shows a single h264 video stream (858x480), duration 10.125 s, and NO audio stream; volumedetect reports 'Output file does not contain any stream'. session.json messages: the user's request, then the question 'Which language?', the answer 'English if there is audible speech', the plan sentence, and then 'check failed: check needs a picture' twice. Nothing was made (assets/tree-2 is empty). The judge correctly failed 'clearly states that the clip has no audible speech' and the unneeded question.
